descriptions.text: Enchanted Venomous Elven Rock Chucker – Contraption. The mounted, fast-attack artillery specialists of the Dream don't bring siege engines with them when they go raiding. That's why they're so annoyingly deadly. Using a combination of knowledge, druid magic, and a little something-something extra—wink—they're able to rapidly construct their war machines on the fly. These can't-take-a-joke beanpoles can conjure up a whole regiment of wall-breaching contraptions in a matter of hours. Translation: you don't want these pale fuckers on your doorstep. This particular light-duty rock thrower is made by casting Bamboozeled on a patch of land and then assembling the device from the resulting poisonous bamboo stalks. …

recap.text: Carl takes the dead hunter's gonorrhea arrow and the green-glowing trebuchet, light enough to carry. A mile from the nearest Odious Creeper, he spikes it into the grass, sends Donut up a tree, pours Mordecai's weedkiller into the cup on the sling, and hits the lever. The System credits Donut with the kill, and she rises two levels to 47.

beats.headline: The real prize
beats.text: The dead hunter's hand is already gone, sent to Carl in a hunter killer box; his loot runs to an unenchanted bow, a gonorrhea arrow and a photograph of Louis with a dog filter. The real prize is the trebuchet, abandoned in the clearing and spiked to the ground, oddly small for the rocks it has been lobbing: the size and height of a windsurfing board, made of a weird, hollow wood, light enough to carry easily, and glowing green. There is no counterweight. Two plates want to come together like magnets; ratchet the arm, attach the rock to the sling, pull the lever. Carl suspects the postage-stamp plates are high tech, not magic. These assholes are still cheating.
beats.gist: The trebuchet is the real prize: a small, light, glowing green, magnet-plated, counterweightless elven cheat.

beats.headline: The cup on the sling
beats.text: Carl's poison delivery system was over-engineered. The rock chucker's Poison Cloud is not self-contained after all: pour a potion into the little cup on the side of the sling and it changes the delivery poison. There still has to be a projectile, and he has plenty of three-hundred-pound rocks. In the rain and mud, a mile short of the nearest Odious Creeper, he spikes the trebuchet into the grass while Donut climbs so high up a tree that he cannot see her. He has no idea how to aim it, so the first rock goes without the potion: she can tell him if it is close.
beats.gist: Carl spikes the rock chucker into the grass while Donut climbs a tree; the first rock flies plain.

beats.headline: The spotter takes the credit
beats.text: Next attack will contain the poison, Carl writes, and if it works he can keep his garbage can poison bombs for something else. He adds Mordecai's weedkiller to the trebuchet and hits the lever. You hit it perfectly, Donut reports; the green stuff is getting messed up by the rain. A few seconds after the shot, the System announces that an Odious Creeper has fallen and Crawler Princess Donut has been given credit for the kill. Thirty remain, and she is up two levels to 47. Mordecai says he forgot to mention that the spotter usually gets the lion's share of credit with siege equipment. Forgot my ass, Carl thinks.
beats.gist: Carl adds weedkiller to the trebuchet, and Donut gets the Odious Creeper kill credit.
